title: Interests
bigQuestion: How do our interests change over time?
summary: Students learn words for music, events and hobbies, ask How long ...? with the present perfect and since / for, compare the present perfect with the simple past and just, make nouns with -ion, and learn to respect other people's interests.
warmup: What do you like doing in your free time?
Do you play a musical instrument?
What did you like doing when you were younger?
What does your best friend like doing?

grammar.title: Present Perfect Questions with since / for
grammar.rule: Use the present perfect (have / has + past participle) for something that started in the past and is still true now. Use “for” with a length of time (for two years) and “since” with a starting point (since 2020, since Monday). To ask about the length of time, say “How long have you ...?”
grammar.form: How long + have / has + subject + past participle? | have / has + past participle + for (a length of time) / since (a starting point)
examples: How long have you played the oud?
I've played the oud for three years.
Nouf has been a member of the chess club since September.
Has Omar collected stamps for a long time?

items.prompt: I have played the drums ___ two years.
items.explanation: “Two years” is a length of time, so we use for.

items.prompt: Sara has lived in Jeddah ___ 2019.
items.explanation: 2019 is the starting point, so we use since.

items.prompt: How long ___ Fahad been a member of the club?
items.explanation: With he / she / it (Fahad), we use has.

items.prompt: How long have you ___ the violin?
items.explanation: After have / has we use the past participle: played.

items.prompt: Which one goes with “since”?
items.explanation: “Last summer” is a starting point, so we say since last summer.

items.prompt: Which one goes with “for”?
items.explanation: “Six months” is a length of time, so we say for six months.

items.prompt: We have known each other ___ we were six.
items.explanation: “We were six” is a starting point, so we use since.

items.prompt: Reem has collected stamps ___ a long time.
items.explanation: “A long time” is a length of time, so we use for.

items.prompt: How long ___ you had your oud?
items.explanation: With you, we use have: How long have you had ...?

items.prompt: Khalid ___ interested in chess since he was eight.
items.explanation: Present perfect of be with he: has been.

items.prompt: They ___ their music teacher for five years.
items.explanation: know – knew – known. With they: have known.

items.prompt: My cousins ___ us since the festival.
items.explanation: Negative present perfect: have not (haven't) + past participle.

items.prompt: How long has she ___ poetry?
items.explanation: write – wrote – written. After has we use written (or been writing).

items.answer: How long have you played the drums?
items.explanation: How long + have + you + past participle?

items.answer: I have collected stamps for three years.
items.explanation: have + past participle + for + length of time.

items.answer: She has been a member since January.
items.explanation: has been + since + starting point.

items.answer: Has he lived here for a long time?
items.explanation: Yes / no question: Has + subject + past participle ...?

items.prompt: Omar has played the oud for two years.
answer: How long has Omar played the oud?
How long has Omar been playing the oud?
items.explanation: How long + has + Omar + played ...?

items.prompt: Nouf has been a member of the club since May.
answer: How long has Nouf been a member of the club?
items.explanation: How long + has + Nouf + been ...?

items.instruction: Write one sentence with the present perfect and “since”.
items.prompt: Fahad moved to Riyadh in 2020. He still lives there.
answer: Fahad has lived in Riyadh since 2020.
Fahad has been living in Riyadh since 2020.
He has lived in Riyadh since 2020.
items.explanation: It started in 2020 and is still true: has lived + since 2020.

items.prompt: I have played chess since the summer.
answer: I have not played chess since the summer.
I haven't played chess since the summer.
items.explanation: Put not after have: have not (haven't) played.

items.sentence: I have played chess since three years.
items.answer: I have played chess for three years.
items.explanation: “Three years” is a length of time, so use for, not since.

items.sentence: How long has she had her violin?
items.answer: How long has she had her violin?
items.explanation: Correct! How long + has + she + had?

items.sentence: How long you have played the drum?
items.answer: How long have you played the drum?
items.explanation: In a question, have comes before the subject: have you.

items.sentence: She have been a member for two months.
items.answer: She has been a member for two months.
items.explanation: With she, use has, not have.

items.sentence: We have known Sara since we were in first grade.
items.answer: We have known Sara since we were in first grade.
items.explanation: Correct! since + a starting point (we were in first grade).

grammar.title: Present Perfect vs. Simple Past with just
grammar.rule: Use the present perfect (have / has + past participle) for things that started in the past and are still true now, or for things you have never done. Use the simple past for finished actions at a finished time (yesterday, last week, ago). For something that happened a very short time ago, we can say “just” + past verb: I just finished.
grammar.form: Present perfect: have / has (never) + past participle | Simple past: subject + (just) + past verb (+ yesterday / last week / two days ago)
examples: I just returned from the concert.
Sara went to the festival last week.

items.prompt: I ___ the pyramids last year.
items.explanation: “Last year” is a finished time, so we use the simple past.

items.prompt: Nouf has ___ been to a jazz concert.
items.explanation: We use never with the present perfect for something not done in your life.

items.prompt: We ___ in this house since 2018.
items.explanation: “Since 2018” means it started then and is still true: have lived.

items.prompt: Fahad ___ won a prize! He's so happy.
items.explanation: “Just” shows something happened a very short time ago.

items.prompt: Which sentence talks about a finished time in the past?
options: I have never read a poetry book.
I have been a member for a year.
items.explanation: “Yesterday” is a finished time, so the sentence uses the simple past.

items.prompt: “Where's Reem?” “She ___ left. You missed her!”
items.explanation: She left a moment ago, so we say “just left”.

items.prompt: I ___ my puzzle five minutes ago.
items.explanation: “Ago” shows a finished time, so we use the simple past: finished.

items.prompt: My father ___ an experiment like this.
items.explanation: For something not done in your life: has never + past participle.

items.prompt: Great news! We just ___ an invitation to the festival!
items.explanation: just + past verb: get → got.

items.prompt: Omar ___ chess since he was seven.
items.explanation: “Since he was seven” means it is still true now: has played.

items.prompt: Last night, I ___ to bed at midnight.
items.explanation: “Last night” is a finished time: go → went.

items.prompt: Look! Sara ___ me a message.
items.explanation: It happened a moment ago: just sent (or has just sent).

items.answer: I just returned from the concert.
items.explanation: subject + just + past verb for a very recent action.

items.answer: She has never played the violin.
items.explanation: has + never + past participle.

items.answer: We went to the festival last week.
alt: Last week we went to the festival.
items.explanation: Simple past with a finished time (last week).
Present perfect question about experience: Have + you + ever + past participle?

items.instruction: Add “just” to show it happened a moment ago.
items.prompt: The concert started.
items.explanation: Put just before the verb: The concert just started.

items.prompt: I have played the oud.
answer: I have never played the oud.
items.explanation: Put never between have and the past participle.

items.instruction: Change it to the simple past. Add “yesterday” at the end.
items.prompt: Reem has read the magazine.
items.explanation: With yesterday we use the simple past: read (it sounds like “red”).

items.prompt: Khalid has won a prize.
answer: Has Khalid ever won a prize?
items.explanation: Move has to the start: Has Khalid won ...?

items.sentence: I have visited AlUla last year.
items.explanation: “Last year” is a finished time, so use the simple past, not the present perfect.

items.sentence: She has never been to a classical concert.
items.answer: She has never been to a classical concert.
items.explanation: Correct! has never + past participle (been).
The action is finished, so the verb needs the past form: finished.

items.sentence: He has lived in Riyadh since 2015.
items.answer: He has lived in Riyadh since 2015.
items.explanation: Correct! It started in 2015 and is still true.

items.sentence: Omar have just won a prize.
items.answer: Omar has just won a prize.
items.explanation: With he / she / it (Omar), use has, not have.

reading.title: The Oud in the Window
reading.text:
Khalid was bored. It was the summer vacation, and he had nothing to do. His sister Nouf was busy with her chess puzzles, and his little brother was playing a game online.

One afternoon, Khalid walked past a music shop in the old market. In the window, he saw a beautiful oud. He stood and looked at it for a long time.

That evening, he told his grandfather about it. Grandpa smiled and went to his room. He came back with an old oud. “I have played this instrument since I was your age,” he said. “Do you want to learn?”

Khalid has taken oud lessons with his grandfather for two years now. He practices every day after school. Last month, he played traditional songs at a school concert, and he won a prize!

Not everyone in his family loves music. Nouf prefers chess, and she has been a member of the chess club since January. Khalid doesn't really enjoy chess, but he never laughs at her hobby. “Everyone has different interests,” Grandpa says. “We should respect them.” So Khalid sometimes plays chess with Nouf at home, and Nouf listens when he practices the oud.

questions.explanation: Khalid sometimes plays chess with Nouf at home, and she listens when he practices.

reading.title: My Changing Interests
reading.text:
Hi Sara,

How are you? I just got your e-mail, and I loved the photos of your stamp collection! You asked me about my interests. Well, they have changed a lot this year.

When I was nine, I collected stamps too. I have about two hundred stamps, and my favorite one has a picture of the pyramids. But I don't collect them anymore. Now I'm interested in poetry. I have written poems since last summer, and I read a poetry magazine every month.

I have also been a member of the science club for six months. Last week, we did an amazing experiment with lemons and electricity. It was the best club meeting ever!

Guess what? I just won a prize in a poetry competition! There is a festival at the culture center next Thursday, and I'm going to read my poem there at midday. I've attached an invitation. Can you come?

Write back soon!
Nouf

reading.title: Sara and Her Violin
reading.text:
This month, our school magazine talked to Sara Almutairi from Grade 6. She plays the violin in a music group for girls in Jeddah.

Magazine: How long have you played the violin, Sara?
Sara: I have played it for four years. I started when I was eight.

Magazine: Why did you choose the violin?
Sara: When I was little, my father took me to a classical concert. I heard the violins, and I loved them! After the concert, I asked my parents for lessons.

Magazine: Have you ever played other instruments?
Sara: Yes. I tried the drums last year, but they were too loud for me! I have also played a little jazz on the piano.

Magazine: How long have you been a member of the music group?
Sara: I've been a member since last September. We practice every Saturday.

Magazine: Have you won any prizes?
Sara: Yes! I just won second prize in an online music competition. I recorded my music at home and sent it.

Magazine: What's next?
Sara: Our group is going to play at a music festival in March. We will play classical music and some traditional Saudi songs, too.

Magazine: Thank you, Sara, and good luck!

questions.explanation: Sara says, “I have played it for four years.”

It is a plan for the future.
questions.answer: It is a finished action at a finished time.
questions.explanation: We use the simple past for finished actions at a finished time, like “when I was eight”.

reading.title: Piece by Piece
reading.text:
Hi! My name is Fahad, and welcome to my puzzle blog. I have loved puzzles since I was six years old. My grandfather gave me my first puzzle. It had only fifty pieces!

Now I'm twelve, and I have finished more than a hundred puzzles. My biggest one has 1,000 pieces. It shows the pyramids in Egypt. It took me three weeks, and I finished it at midnight on the last day of the summer vacation. My mom wasn't very happy about that!

I don't only do picture puzzles. I have also done the word puzzles in a children's magazine for two years. Every month, the magazine has a puzzle competition. Last month, I sent my answers. And guess what? I just got an e-mail from the magazine. I won the prize! It's a new puzzle of the rocks at AlUla.

Some of my friends think puzzles are boring. They get bored when they can't find the right piece. But for me, puzzles are like science experiments. You try something, and if it doesn't work, you try again.

Have you ever done a puzzle with your family? Tell me in the comments below!

reading.title: Come to Our Club Festival!
reading.text:
Our boys' school has had interest clubs for ten years, and this year we are going to celebrate with a Club Festival! It will be on Wednesday, April 15, from 9 o'clock until midday. All families are welcome. Every boy will bring home an invitation this week.

What can you see at the festival?

The Music Club has just bought new traditional drums. The boys have practiced for six weeks, and they are going to play in the main hall at 10 o'clock.

The Science Club will show some exciting experiments. Last year, their volcano experiment won first prize at the city science fair!

The Chess Club has been open since 2019. Visitors can play a game against our best members.

The Poetry Club will read poems about the Red Sea.

The Stamp Club has collected over 3,000 stamps from 80 countries. You can see them in the library.

Mr. Ibrahim, our principal, says, “Our clubs help boys find new interests. Nobody is bored at our school!”

You can't come? No problem. We will put photos of the festival online next week.

wordWork.title: The suffix -ion
wordWork.rule: We can add -ion to some verbs to make nouns: collect → collection, invent → invention. If the verb ends in -e, drop the e first: create → creation. Some words change a little more: invite → invitation.

items.prompt: Thank you for the ___ to your party!
items.explanation: invite → invitation. This word adds -ation.

items.prompt: Reem has a big stamp ___.
items.explanation: collect + -ion → collection.

items.prompt: The telephone was an amazing ___.
items.explanation: invent + -ion → invention.

items.prompt: What is the noun of “correct”?
items.explanation: correct + -ion → correction. It is a noun.

items.prompt: Our family had a big ___ for Eid.
items.explanation: celebrate: drop the e and add -ion → celebration.

items.prompt: Which word is a noun?
items.explanation: Words ending in -ion are usually nouns: decoration.

items.prompt: Can you give me some ___ about the festival?
items.explanation: inform → information. This word adds -ation.

items.prompt: Which verb drops its final “e” before adding -ion?
items.explanation: Create ends in e, so we drop it: creation.

items.prompt: Sunscreen gives your skin ___ from the sun.
items.explanation: protect + -ion → protection.

writing.prompt: Write an e-mail to a friend about how your interests have changed.
writing.hint: Use: Before, I liked ... but now I prefer ..., I've been interested in ... for / since ..., I just ..., I've never tried ...
writing.model:
Hi Omar,

My interests have changed a lot! Before, I liked video games, but now I prefer football. I've been a member of the school team since September. Last week, I scored my first goal, and I just got new football boots! I also like puzzles. I've done puzzles for three years. I've never tried chess, but I want to learn. Can you teach me?

Fahad

writing.prompt: Write about the hobby of someone in your family.
writing.hint: Who is it? What is the hobby? How long has he / she done it? Use: for / since, has never ..., just ...
writing.model: My grandmother loves poetry. She has written poems since she was a young girl. That is more than fifty years! She has never won a prize, but our family loves her poems. She just wrote a new poem about Riyadh, and she read it to us at dinner.
